Q26.purpose: Conversion rate (orders per session) by channel for P001 in Aug vs Sep
Q26.sql:
WITH orders_month AS (
    SELECT date_format(o.date, 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
           o.channel,
           COUNT(*) AS order_cnt
    FROM WHYDROP_FILES.orders o
    WHERE o.product_id = 'P001'
      AND o.date >= '2026-08-01'
      AND o.date < '2026-09-01'
    GROUP BY month, o.channel
),
sessions_month AS (
    SELECT date_format(wt.date, 'yyyy-MM') AS month,
           wt.source AS channel,
           SUM(wt.sessions) AS session_cnt
    FROM WHYDROP_FILES.web_traffic wt
    WHERE wt.date >= '2026-08-01'
      AND wt.date < '2026-09-01'
    GROUP BY month, wt.source
)
SELECT o.month,
       o.channel,
       o.order_cnt,
       s.session_cnt,
       CASE WHEN s.session_cnt = 0 THEN 0 ELSE o.order_cnt / s.session_cnt END AS conversion_rate
FROM orders_month o
JOIN sessions_month s

memory_recalled.content: [Why did Notion Freelance OS sales fall even though we raised the price?] VERIFIED CAUSE: The price increase for Notion Freelance OS suppressed demand: unit orders fell by more than the price rose, so gross sales dropped despite a higher unit price. - The $19 to $29 price hike on 2026-09-01 raised price ~53% but orders fell ~57% (269 to 115), so gross revenue dropped from 5111.0 to 3335.0 despite the higher unit price. (conf 0.97, queries Q4,Q5,Q6)

[Why did Notion Freelance OS sales fall even though we raised the price?] REJECTED: The price hike was geographically concentrated: buyers in price-sensitive countries (e.g., IN, GB) stopped purchasing P001 after 2026-09-01 while US buyers held up, so total sales fell. - H5 is rejected: the P001 price hike was uniform across all six countries ($19 → $29, +52.6%) and the US actually had the steepest order decline (−62.4%), so the sales drop was broad-based rather than concentrated in price-sensitive markets.

[Why did Notion Freelance OS sales fall even though we raised the price?] VERIFIED CAUSE: The $19→$29 price increase for Notion Freelance OS (P001) on 2026-09-01 suppressed demand: unit orders fell by more than the price rose, so gross sales dropped despite the higher unit price. - The $19→$29 price increase for P001 on 2026-09-01 coincided with a 57% order drop (vs 28% for control group) and a 35% revenue decline, indicating price-driven demand suppression. (conf 0.98, queries Q17,Q19,Q21)

[Why did Notion Freelance OS sales fall even though we raised the price?] REJECTED: The sales decline was concentrated in specific countries due to local seasonality or purchasing-power sensitivity to the higher price, not a global demand drop. - The sales decline was broad-based across all six countries (every market fell 23.68%–42.56%), not concentrated in specific countries, so H6 is not supported.

[Why did Notion Freelance OS sales fall even though we raised the price?] REJECTED: Post-hike refunds and 'bought by mistake' / 'changed mind' disputes spiked for P001, eroding net revenue and deterring new buyers after 2026-09-01. - P001 refund counts and support tickets for 'bought by mistake'/'changed mind' did not spike after the 2026-09-01 price hike; net revenue fell mainly because gross revenue collapsed, not because of refund erosion.
